title: PNT Density Asymptotic for Prime Gaps in Short Intervals
description: While Bertrand's Postulate guarantees a prime in (n, 2n] and Baker-Harman-Pintz (2001) prove existence in [x, x+x^0.525], the deeper question is whether primes are distributed with PNT-predicted *density* in short intervals: π(x+h) - π(x) ~ h/ln(x). This formalization formalizes the ShortIntervalPNT property, proves density implies existence, and establishes the RH-conditional result for h ≥ x^(1/2+ε).

overview.historicalContext:
The Prime Number Theorem (PNT, 1896) tells us $\pi(x) \sim x/\ln x$: primes up to $x$ are approximately $x/\ln x$ in number. A natural refinement asks: how are primes distributed in short intervals $[x, x+h]$ for $h \ll x$? The PNT heuristic predicts $h/\ln x$ primes in such an interval. Whether this asymptotic actually holds — and for which $h$ — is the *short interval density question*.

Two distinct answers exist: **existence** (does the interval contain *at least one* prime?) and **density** (does the interval contain *approximately $h/\ln x$* primes?). Baker-Harman-Pintz (2001) proved existence for $h = x^{0.525}$. The density question is harder: under the Riemann Hypothesis, von Koch's bound $|\pi(x) - \text{Li}(x)| = O(\sqrt{x} \log x)$ implies density holds for $h = x^{1/2+\varepsilon}$. Unconditionally, Huxley (1972) proved density for $h = x^{7/12+\varepsilon}$, and the current record stands at $h = x^{0.525+\varepsilon}$ (matching BHP) for the density statement.

This formalization introduces formal Lean 4 infrastructure for the density question, proves the implication density $\Rightarrow$ existence (a mathematical tautology), and formalizes the RH-conditional result as an axiom.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (OQ-04)**: For what values of $\theta < 1/2$ does the density asymptotic $\pi(x + x^\theta) - \pi(x) \sim x^\theta / \ln x$ hold as $x \to \infty$?

**Known unconditionally**: Existence (at least one prime) in $[x, x+x^{0.525}]$ — Baker-Harman-Pintz 2001.
**Known under RH**: Density holds for all $\theta > 1/2$ — von Koch's error bound.
**Open**: Does density hold unconditionally for any $\theta < 1/2$? What is the threshold?
overview.text: A 323-line formalization formalizing the *density* perspective on prime gaps in short intervals. Defines `ShortIntervalPNT θ` as the statement that the density ratio $(\pi(x+x^\theta) - \pi(x)) \cdot \ln(x) / x^\theta \to 1$ as $x \to \infty$. Proves that `ShortIntervalPNT θ` implies prime existence in $[x, x+x^\theta]$ for all large $x$ — formalized via filter reasoning on `Nat.primeCounting`. The key `primeCounting_lt_implies_prime_exists` lemma directly constructs a prime from a jump in the counting function using `Nat.count_eq_card_filter_range`. Also proves `long_interval_density_from_pnt`: for constant $c > 0$, the density $(\pi((1+c)x) - \pi(x)) \cdot \ln(x) / (cx) \to 1$ follows from PNT alone (2 sorries in filter algebra). The RH-conditional result that density holds for $\theta > 1/2$ is axiomatized as `shortIntervalPNT_rh_conditional`.
overview.proofStrategy: The density-implies-existence direction (the core new theorem) works by: (1) assuming `shortIntervalDensityRatio > 0` eventually (from density → 1), (2) deducing `primePi(x + x^θ) > primePi(x)` via positivity of log and interval length, (3) casting to `Nat.primeCounting` and applying `primeCounting_lt_implies_prime_exists` (proved by Finset card monotonicity), (4) converting the floor bounds to real-valued bounds. For the log ratio lemma, write `log(x)/log((1+c)x) = 1/(1 + log(1+c)/log(x))` and use `tendsto_const_nhds.div_atTop Real.tendsto_log_atTop`.
keyInsights: Density asymptotic (π(x+h) - π(x) ~ h/ln x) is strictly stronger than existence (at least one prime in [x, x+h])
ShortIntervalPNT θ for any fixed θ implies PrimeGapConjecture θ holds for all sufficiently large x — formalized via filter eventually
The primeCounting_lt_implies_prime_exists lemma: a strict increase in π automatically yields a prime via Finset cardinality
log(x)/log((1+c)x) → 1 is proved by writing it as 1/(1 + log(1+c)/log(x)) and using log(x) → ∞
Under RH, von Koch's bound gives the density asymptotic for intervals of length x^(1/2+ε) — the best conditional result
The existence-density gap is the central open problem: BHP gives existence at 0.525, but density at 0.525 remains open unconditionally
prerequisites: Filter convergence in Lean 4 (Tendsto, atTop, nhds)
Analytic number theory (zero-free regions, explicit formula)

sections.title: Module Header and Imports
sections.summary: Imports from Mathlib (prime counting, asymptotics, log, filters) and parent modules (PrimeNumberTheorem, BertrandsPostulateOQ03).
sections.mathContext: Builds on `BertrandsPostulateOQ03` (PrimeGapConjecture, BHP axiom) and `PrimeNumberTheorem` (π(x)·log(x)/x → 1, RH axiom).

sections.title: Counting Lemma — Prime Existence from Counting Jump
sections.summary: primeCounting_lt_implies_prime_exists: a strict increase in Nat.primeCounting implies a prime in the gap.
sections.mathContext: If $\pi(m) < \pi(n)$, there must be a prime $p$ with $m < p \leq n$. Proved by contradiction: if no such prime exists, then by Finset.card_le_card the counting function cannot increase.

sections.title: ShortIntervalPNT Definition
sections.summary: shortIntervalDensityRatio: the normalized prime count ratio. ShortIntervalPNT θ: this ratio → 1 as x → ∞.

sections.title: Density Implies Existence (Main Theorem)
sections.summary: shortIntervalPNT_implies_primeGapConjecture_eventually: ShortIntervalPNT θ implies prime existence in [x, x+x^θ] for all large x.
sections.mathContext: From density → 1: ratio > 0 eventually → count difference > 0 eventually → a prime exists in the gap. The key step: convert real-valued positivity to nat primeCounting strict inequality via floor bounds and cast.

sections.title: Log Ratio Lemma
sections.summary: log_ratio_tendsto_one: log(x)/log((1+c)x) → 1 for any c > 0. Used in the PNT composition for long intervals.

sections.title: Long Interval Density from PNT (2 sorries)
sections.summary: long_interval_density_from_pnt: for c > 0, (π((1+c)x) - π(x))·log(x)/(cx) → 1 follows from PNT. Two sorries remain in filter limit algebra.
sections.mathContext: Apply PNT to $(1+c)x$: $\pi((1+c)x) \cdot \ln((1+c)x)/((1+c)x) \to 1$. Multiply by $\ln(x)/\ln((1+c)x) \to 1$ to get $\pi((1+c)x) \cdot \ln(x)/((1+c)x) \to 1$. Subtract PNT for $x$: $(\pi((1+c)x) - \pi(x)) \cdot \ln(x)/(cx) \to 1$.

sections.title: RH-Conditional Short Interval PNT (Axiom)
sections.mathContext: Under RH: $|\pi(x) - \text{Li}(x)| = O(\sqrt{x} \log x)$ (von Koch 1901). For $h = x^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, this error is $o(h/\ln x)$, so the density ratio $\to 1$.

sections.title: BHP-Density Separation and Summary
sections.summary: bhp_vs_density_gap: BHP gives existence at 0.525 and ShortIntervalPNT(0.525) implies density. prime_density_in_short_intervals_summary collects all results.
sections.mathContext: Separation: BHP proves existence (at least one prime), while ShortIntervalPNT proves density (~ x^0.525/ln x primes). Whether the density statement holds at 0.525 unconditionally is open.

conclusion.summary: This entry formalizes the distinction between prime existence and prime density in short intervals, proves density implies existence, and conditionally establishes density for intervals of length x^(1/2+ε) under RH.
conclusion.implications: The central open question — whether density holds unconditionally at the BHP exponent 0.525 — separates two natural strengthenings of BHP. Resolving it likely requires new zero-density estimates for the Riemann zeta function beyond current methods.
openQuestions: Does ShortIntervalPNT(0.525) hold unconditionally? (Would strengthen BHP from existence to density)
What is the infimum of θ for which ShortIntervalPNT(θ) holds unconditionally?
Can long_interval_density_from_pnt be fully proved in Lean without sorries using Mathlib's filter algebra?
Is there a Lean-provable θ < 1 for which ShortIntervalPNT holds, using only Mathlib's current PNT?

crossReferences.description: Parent entry (OQ-03) formalizes the prime gap existence question (PrimeGapConjecture θ). This OQ-04 adds the density perspective: ShortIntervalPNT θ asks for the asymptotic count, not just existence.
PNT (π(x) ~ x/ln x) is the foundation. ShortIntervalPNT asks whether PNT refines to short intervals: π(x+h) - π(x) ~ h/ln x.
Bertrand's Postulate is the crude θ=1 case: prime existence in [x, 2x]. The density question generalizes to smaller intervals.
